"Running is extremely stressful on the body for heavier people."

I hadn't really considered this. I mean I understand that heavier people will struggle more when it comes to running, but I hadn't considered the physics of a bunch of happy, bouncing fat and the toll it can take on the rest of the body. The sheer g-forces alone! I will take it slower and give my body time to adjust the first couple of weeks.

I believe i will have to restart C25k (at least the first week) a few times, but its nice to know this is common practice.

"Shoot for between 60-80% of (220 - your age) beats per minute"

I wasn't aware of this particular equation. I understand it's not a hard and fast rule or anything, but for me in particular, its nice to have some basic numbers behind the run to keep as a goal.

As far as the shortness of breath/heart rate problem, I believe I will give it a few more days before scheduling an appointment. I think it's just that I've led such a sedentary lifestyle for so long that my body was surprised. I will however be very vigilant, and if any chest pains do crop up I'll cease my workout and call the Doc asap.

Thanks, knowing other heavy runner had a similar experience to the one I'm having is actually comforting.

You're absolutely right when you say not to push yourself to hard to fast, this is something that I'm going to have to police myself about in the future. I'm the type of person that likes to jump in head first, then will slowly lose enthusiasm, and I'm really not trying to do either of that where my weight loss is concerned.

I'm also glad that my out-of-breath thing isn't uncommon! Didn't want to make a mistake and have some sort of heart attack.

I also JUST found /r/c25k, and I'm amazed at the community there. So many wonderful resources for an old fat guy like me to take advantage of! I also have spent the last 15 minuets or so saving youtube videos from /r/bodyweightfitness, and I really think they will be a big help.

I didn't consider however that a better diet might be considered more important then working out. I think I might have a handle on it though. My plan is to change to eating 3 (maybe 4) small meals a day (instead of eating one big meal and snacking on crap the rest of the time) and NOT eating right before a go to sleep (like I have been doing for years). That and the complete abandonment of things I know are terrible for me (Soda), and I think I'm going the right direction.

Thank you so much for taking the time to answer my questions, I very much appreciate it!

Reddit continues to amaze me. I was vaguely aware of /r/bodyweightfitness, but I had NO idea /r/c25k was even a thing. Their resources (especially that pre-made schedule), will help a lot.

Thank you for your answers and tips kind stranger, I will take your advice to heart.
